key_takeaway: IME queries contextual text and selection; `textupdate` updates shared buffer; apps must avoid `updateText()` during `textupdate`; apps must call selection/layout updates for selection, scroll, and IME candidate placement.
Text input is decoupled from DOM mutation; beforeinput remains intent for commands; native selection/caret are hard and often require app-owned visual selection.
Typing updates EditContext text and view model without DOM mutation; deletion uses `textupdate` selection and empty beforeinput target ranges; backward selections are exercised.
Selection supports backward endpoints; control/selection/character bounds are explicit API calls and invalid argument behavior is tested.
When focus moves away from the associated element, EditContext stops receiving text updates and normal input receives keystrokes.

VS Code updates EditContext text/selection from model state, maps textupdate to type/composition operations, renders IME text formats as decorations, and updates scroll-adjusted selection/control/character bounds from cached layout data.
Production fallback special-cases macOS long press, Android composition data, blur/tap without compositionend, paste/cut selectionchange ignore windows, and noisy selectionchange bursts.
